source.title: The Forbidden Throw
source.summary: How the Prophet banned bay' al-gharar, and why the Arabic word for dice became the English word "hazard."
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: The English word "hazard" comes from al-zahr, Arabic for dice. But in Islamic law, the concept goes far deeper than gambling. The Prophet Muhammad explicitly banned bay' al-gharar: transactions built on excessive uncertainty, where one party doesn't know what they're really buying. This episode traces the origins of this prohibition in the Quran and Hadith, explains why early Islamic jurists considered it as fundamental as the ban on riba, and shows how 7th-century contract law was already solving problems that would crash modern financial markets fourteen centuries later.
